Manage and refer urgently:
If short of breath or oxygen saturation < 95%, give oxygen: 1-4L/min via nasal prongs or 6-10L/min via facemask, up to 10-15L/min via non-rebreather mask. Aim for oxygen saturation ≥ 90%.
If tension pneumothorax likely: insert large bore cannula2 above 6th rib, anterior axillary line. Arrange urgent chest tube.
If shock/systolic BP < 80, give sodium chloride 0.9% 500mL IV over 30 minutes, repeat until systolic BP > 80. Continue 1L 6 hourly. Stop if breathing worsens.
If severe pneumonia (2 or more of: confusion/decreased level of consciousness, BP < 90/60, RR ≥ 30 or age > 65): give ceftriaxone3 1g IV/IM.
If rapid deep breathing, check fingerprick glucose. If > 11.1 19.

cough, shortness of breath
Pneumocystis pneumonia

(PJP) likely • Doctor to confirm on chest x-ray. • If > 56kg, give co- trimoxazole 320/1600mg, 6 hourly for 3 weeks. If < 56kg, reduce dose5. • Give HIV routine care 126. • Refer same day if: x-ray atypical/unavailable, shortness of breath on mild exertion or RR > 24.
If diagnosis uncertain or poor response to treatment, refer. If patient has life-limiting illness, also give palliative care 191.

Approach to the patient with cough or difficulty breathing not needing urgent attention • Test for HIV 124. If on abacavir, check for abacavir hypersensitivity reaction (AHR) 131. • Test for TB: send 1 sputum sample for TB NAAT 102. • If patient smokes, encourage to stop 164. Ask about duration and recurrence of cough or difficulty breathing:
Cough < 2 weeks and not recurrent
Does patient have crackles or bronchial breathing on auscultation?

No: Acute viral infection likely • Usually sudden onset fever, chills or body pain. • If recent cold and now tight/ sore chest or coughing sputum, acute bronchitis likely. • Advise antibiotics are not needed. • If pain/fever: give paracetamol 500mg-1g 4-6 hourly (max 4g/24 hours) as needed for up to 5 days. • Advise rest and hydration. • Advise patient to return if earache, pain over sinuses, or cough/fever persists longer than 1 week.
